title: DDS Weekly Maritime Intelligence — Issue 001
excerpt: The inaugural issue of DDS Weekly Maritime Intelligence — covering crude and product tanker markets, Singapore and global bunker pricing, sanctions and compliance watch, and weekly fixtures across Southeast Asia.
ceoQuote: The present tanker market is not simply a freight market; it is a risk-allocation market.

title: DDS Weekly Maritime Intelligence — Issue 002
excerpt: This week's issue examines the de-escalation around the Strait of Hormuz against a backdrop of still-elevated physical and route risk, alongside the usual market, bunker, and compliance intelligence.
ceoQuote: A falling oil price is not the same thing as a falling risk. This week, the gap between the two is the whole story.
highlights: Hormuz de-escalation vs. elevated physical risk
Sanctions / Compliance Watch — DDS Compliance Rating

title: DDS Weekly Maritime Intelligence — Issue 003
excerpt: The Hormuz blockade turns kinetic: a US Navy engagement, a Gard P&I war-risk cancellation across the Indian Ocean, Gulf of Aden and Red Sea, and the return of full Baltic Exchange freight data.
ceoQuote: Two weeks ago the market was pricing a Hormuz deal. This week the US Navy fired on a ship trying to reach Iran. That is the distance between headline and reality in this trade.
highlights: US Navy engagement turns the Hormuz blockade kinetic
Gard P&I war-risk cancellation across the Indian Ocean, Gulf of Aden and Red Sea
Full Baltic Exchange freight-rate breakdown restored

title: DDS Weekly Maritime Intelligence — Issue 004
excerpt: The Islamabad MoU lapses: a crew fatality aboard MINOAN DIGNITY, the first Iranian seizure since June, and over 100 VLCCs withdrawn from Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb on Beijing's guidance.
ceoQuote: A chief engineer went to work this week and did not come home. Before we talk about worldscale points, we should sit with that.
highlights: MoU lapses; Iran asserts a transit permit-and-toll regime
Crew fatality aboard MINOAN DIGNITY; tanker AMARA seized
100+ VLCCs withdrawn from Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb
Zombie tanker fleet linked to Malaysia's Riau outer port limits

title: DDS Weekly Maritime Intelligence — Issue 005
excerpt: A calmer week: no new casualty or seizure, reported Iran-Oman progress on managed transit, and a joint pledge from Malaysia, Singapore and Indonesia to keep the Malacca and Singapore Straits open.
ceoQuote: A quieter week is not the same as a settled one. We should read it that way.
highlights: No new casualty or seizure — risk level down from Critical to Elevated
Iran-Oman reported close to a managed Hormuz transit framework
Malaysia, Singapore & Indonesia pledge to keep the Straits open under UNCLOS
VLCC TCE holds above US$330,000/day despite the calmer tone
Container majors test a partial return to the Suez route
